key_insight: Embedding an asymptotic boundary-layer corrector in a neural solver preserves accuracy at small viscosity without requiring a grid that resolves the layer.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce training costs for low-viscosity flow simulations by representing thin wall layers analytically rather than resolving them numerically.
method: Enrich a physics-informed neural network with the asymptotic corrector for the vorticity layer of width √ε.
Tie the corrector amplitude to the network’s wall trace, avoiding prior knowledge of the limit solution.
Use coarse-grid finite-volume flux differences for the Laplacian to obtain the sl-FVNN variant.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports uniform accuracy across six decades of viscosity for Stokes and Navier–Stokes tests, with sl-FVNN matching sl-PINN accuracy within random-seed scatter at about half the per-step training cost.
watch_item: The reported results concern two-dimensional flows with slip boundary conditions; extension to other wall conditions or three-dimensional flows is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Singular layer neural networks for the Navier-Stokes equations at small viscosity
